question: Is signed-query HME, with its existing field bias retained, equivalent to exact signed-cosine NN within one percentage point at the registered primary condition?

dataset.distribution: Independent standard-normal real vectors, generated by default_rng(seed).
dataset.preprocessing: Reuse the frozen HME-NN-1 helpers: Hann-windowed and normalized stored vectors; native unwindowed queries or symmetric Hann-windowed queries, identical across arms.
dataset.side_information: Every record and query has the same position. NN retains the same records and lineage. No search receives a target ID or useful target position.

intervention: HME_abs is the current unmodified default engine. HME_signed replaces exactly float(abs(np.vdot(payload, query_vector)) / denom) with float(np.real(np.vdot(payload, query_vector)) / denom). It retains all other code, including the 0.38/0.42/0.20 weights, query-independent field bias, clipping, threshold, salience defaults, ledger, preprocessing and decoded outputs. Exact NN uses the same processed vectors and stable ties. The signed variant is experimental; the default engine is not changed.

primary.equivalence_rule: Support equivalence only if the paired-seed 90% percentile-bootstrap interval lies strictly inside (-0.01,+0.01), and all arms satisfy the common storage cap. Otherwise equivalence is not established; failure alone does not prove inferiority.
primary.noninferiority_rule: Separately report noninferiority within one percentage point if the same interval's lower endpoint exceeds -0.01. This does not mean HME_signed >= NN without tolerance, and does not replace the primary equivalence criterion.
primary.direction_rule: A 95% interval wholly below zero supports lower mean accuracy; wholly above zero supports higher mean accuracy. A 90% upper endpoint below -0.01 supports a deficit exceeding the equivalence margin. These distinctions are reported even if different labels hold simultaneously.

predictions: Replacing absolute with signed query similarity is expected to improve HME over HME_abs at the primary condition.
Equivalence of HME_signed and NN is a hypothesis, not assumed from the earlier telescoping decomposition. The retained field bias can interact with the changed scoring rule.

secondary.conditions: All noise levels and query modes; primary decision is restricted to native sigma 1.0.
secondary.unmatched: Report acceptance on unrelated Gaussian queries without a designated target; no distribution-shift or calibrated rejection claim.

statistics.unit: Independent corpus/noise seed, with all arms paired within each seed.
statistics.intervals: Percentile paired-seed bootstrap at 5/95 percent (90% interval) for the registered equivalence/noninferiority rule, and 2.5/97.5 percent (95% interval) for effect estimates. This is an approximate bootstrap CI-based equivalence procedure, not a claim of exact finite-sample type-I error control.
statistics.sample_size: Thirty new seeds fixed before execution to improve precision for the one-point margin relative to the ten-seed exploratory comparison. No guaranteed power or seed-count extension if the result is inconclusive.
statistics.multiplicity: One primary equivalence comparison. Other cells and sign-effect contrasts are descriptive; no replacement of the primary or margin revision after outcomes.
statistics.zero_variance: Zero-width intervals describe observed replicates, not population certainty.

budget.accounting: Reuse HME-NN-1 recursive object and owned-array accounting, including records/lineage, with alias deduplication. Excludes interpreter/shared code, allocator overhead and transient query workspace. Same maximum budget and candidate set, not an equal-consumed-byte capacity frontier.

latency.measurement: perf_counter_ns, rotate arm order by (query index+repetition) modulo three, one BLAS thread. Remeasure each arm's public API including preprocessing. HME returns decoded outputs in addition to rankings; NN does not. Record raw timings and per-seed median/p95.

stopping: Execute all thirty seeds and all cells once after the public registration commit. No early stopping, tuning, seed replacement or margin adjustment. Retain FAILURE.json for a technical failure; any correction requires a documented public amendment before a complete rerun, preserving the original registration and failed output.
registration: Publish protocol, evaluator, one-expression variant and correctness fixtures before running any registered seed. Verify their bytes and imported helper/engine bytes against the supplied full registration commit. Record source/generated-module/data hashes and execution times. Preserve the registration commit in Git history.
prior_information: HME-NN-1 outcomes and an eight-item structural fixture at seed 61 were already inspected. They motivate this ablation. No outcomes from the thirty new seeds have been inspected before registration.
